---
title: "Native STACK preparation and cards"
---

Select `cas: maxima` in a STACK block, or set `stack.cas: maxima` in the project
or page settings. Native questions use the owned **runtime-v3**, with
source-loaded STACK at `33383047af39c204bf4442802a058f8b918b2b1b`, for both
author preparation and learner grading. The SymPy backend remains available.

The author path uses Python for the PRT compiler and the common variant review
workflow, Node for the pinned JavaScript grammar frontend and Wasm runner, and
Maxima for mathematical evaluation. PHP is used only in adversarial comparison
tests. Neither PHP, SymPy nor a browser is required for native preparation.
PythonCheckers are a separate continuation capability; they do not execute in
this native backend yet.

## Stage runtime-v3

Use Node 22 or 24 and Python with the installed CTM checker wheels and native
authoring distribution. Obtain `maxima-runtime-v3.json` and
`maxima-runtime-v3.tar.gz` from the owned runtime-v3 GitHub Release, and check out
STACK at the exact revision above. From the component source:

```bash
python scripts/stage-native.py --release /path/to/release-files \
  --stack-source /path/to/pinned-stack --output /path/to/new-native-package
export CTM_STACK_NATIVE_PACKAGE=/path/to/new-native-package
```

Staging verifies the release record, archive, manifest and every runtime/STACK
file. It does not rebuild or modify the runtime, change the release record
format, or change the release archive layout. A missing package is a build
error. Set `CTM_STACK_NODE` if Node is not available as `node`.

The usual `question-variants.py` generate/review/apply commands now use the
selected backend. Maxima owns its seed sequence; these are not imported Moodle
deployments. Approval is required by default. Preview proposals are visibly
unapproved. Publication replays retained candidates, requires current approval,
and checks source/history leases using the same producer as SymPy. A prose edit
refreshes the display while preserving approval; changed mathematics or grading
requires review. Cached native results bind the runtime, STACK pin, compiler,
checker admission wheel, question, seed and Node version; caches do not approve
variants.

## Current capability boundary

The native frontend supports the structural XML importer's bounded algebraic,
numerical and matrix inputs; scoped question/feedback assignments; native
answer tests; weighted PRTs; and basic CASText text, mathematics, input,
validation, feedback, conditionals and comments. Learner expressions use the
same pinned JavaScript admission implementation as the checker payload, with
an additional native serialization allowlist before Maxima evaluation.

Author execution uses an explicit function allowlist independent of STACK's
security-map completeness. `map` and custom `sort` callbacks must be literal
allowlisted first-order functions or inline lambdas. Function names obtained
through variables, lists, strings, `concat` or `sconcat` do not grant executable
authority. Stored lambdas, syntax forms passed as callbacks, `apply` and `at`
remain outside this subset. Strings such as `"none"`, `"red"` and `"real"` are
ordinary data, including in lambda collections, substitutions and answers.

`subst(new, old, expression)` checks actual native operator replacements before
substituting: a new operator must be an allowlisted first-order function
(non-random in feedback). Rewriting lambda or evaluator syntax is unsupported.
`substinpart` accepts positive literal indices only, and `ev` accepts the
supported first-order function flags or `simp`, `numer`, `nouns`, `noeval`.
Author-definition failures are checked before producing candidate evidence.

Unsupported features stop the author build with a diagnostic. These include
PythonChecker continuations and block checkers, arbitrary author function
definitions or execution, JSXGraph, external includes, general CASText blocks
such as `foreach`, CASText question-test inputs (`CT:`), and variable/input
names that collide with protected native functions. An explicitly
rejected feature is not a fallback to SymPy. This is an initial native question
subset, not complete Moodle/STACK compatibility.

Every prepared seed must pass its XML tests and a full-mark teacher-vector
check on every PRT. Wrong-answer probes are retained as author evidence.
Question-test support is bounded by the importer and is not a claim to every
Moodle test sentinel or expectation mode.

Learners validate with the explicit button before grading. Instant validation
is not enabled by this change. One question/variant owns a fresh worker heap;
switching variants retires it. This proves state separation at the cost of
runtime startup on a switch. Loading is outside the calculation clock.
The page needs neither cross-origin isolation nor SharedArrayBuffer. Native
operations do not download or start Pyodide. Pages containing only SymPy cards
do not load the native runtime package.

## Compiler and audit

The PRT compiler is a clean Python implementation with typed IR and a single
active-node transition. The emitted program runs in Maxima; Python and
JavaScript do not interpret the response tree at grading time. The independent
test reference walks paths with Decimal arithmetic. Both our compiler and the
pinned upstream PHP compiler passed the same 120 graphs and 2,572 verdict
assignments against that reference. This tests routing and score arithmetic,
not the mathematical correctness of each answer test.

The [adversarial audit](audits/upstream-compiler-2026-10-27.md) provides two
reproduced upstream rendering defects and one score-precision concern, with
raw evidence and standalone reproduction. Our backend preserves Maxima's
three-decimal PRT score rather than applying upstream PHP's additional
continued-fraction approximation. This compatibility difference is explicit.

The native question CI also exercises actual installed Quarto cards, mixed
backends, full/partial/zero grades, invalid input, XML tests, fresh variant
heaps, shared approvals and stale leases. Six additional authored families
(rational, numerical, matrix, Boolean, nested collections and hyperbolic)
pass 20 XML tests and their full-mark teacher vectors. Literal test decimals
retain trailing zeros, and expected note sequences use upstream's anchoring
rules. Transport replay remains in the separate native foundation workflow.
The full GC stress campaign runs for changes to the call boundary, lifetime,
runtime pin/staging or GC stress test itself, and for manual qualification. Compiler
and card changes use the normal replay, lifecycle and browser gates.
JSXGraph, native Python continuations,
broader input/feedback conformance, locales and offline distribution remain
tracked work.

## Revision and exact replay

`_extensions/ctm-stack/native/stack-pin.json` is the one editable STACK revision.
The workflows, Python tools and grammar generator read it. Run
`node tools/compiler/generate.mjs /path/to/STACK` to regenerate the browser pin,
grammars, metadata and provenance. Refresh the checked source inventories with
their recording tools when upgrading; generated inventories report the pin but
do not configure it. Runtime upgrades still require the owned release gate.

Native operations recreate question variables from the seed on every call,
including teacher validation. They never restore native state from the printed
`env` evidence. This preserves binary float precision and unevaluated structure
even when an author sets `fpprintprec:12`.
